Subject: Scaled commit playbook + SLA credit outline for Acme

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the time earlier today. As requested, attached is a compact playbook that maps three commit tiers to predictable per-token pricing, fallback SLAs, and quick-win operational levers. High level:

- Starter (annual): 25M tokens, baseline per-token price, 3% credit on missed SLOs
- Growth (annual): 250M tokens, mid-tier per-token price, 5% credit + burst buffer
- Enterprise (annual): 1B tokens+, deepest per-token price, 10% credit, guaranteed priority routing

Key differentiators in this offer: we include automatic prefix caching guidance (expected 12–18% token reduction for your chat flows), a 30-day ramp protection window, and an optional quantization profile to reduce unit costs for batched inference. I attached a workbook that shows example blended unit economics under different usage profiles.

Open items I flagged in the workbook:
- Definition of billable token (we propose align to generated + prompt tokens with a 5% tolerance for lower-level logs)
- SLA credit calculation event window (we propose rolling 30-day)
- Procurement timing and DocuSign path

Next steps I suggest:
1) You confirm which tier you want to model (Starter/Growth/Enterprise) and an estimated Q3 ramp profile (conservative/expected/aggressive).
2) If Procurement needs a tracked quote, we’ll attach the worksheet to a formal SOW and send via DocuSign.

Attached: 20260630-proposal-acme-commits.xlsx; SLA-credits-and-fallbacks.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk the workbook with your procurement/legal teams.

Best,
David Kim
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Cell: (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Scaled commit playbook + SLA credit outline for Acme

David —

Thanks for the proposal and the workbook. A few quick questions from procurement/legal before we run numbers:

1) For Enterprise tier, can you confirm whether the 10% credit is capped per quarter or unlimited? Our finance team needs a cap to model exposure.
2) Is there an option to split commitments across regions (US/EU) for data residency reasons?
3) We need a simple definition of "burst buffer" (how many tokens, duration) and whether bursts count against committed volume or are billed separately.

Also, pricing on the workbook looks straightforward but can you provide a short example invoice calc for the Growth tier with a 3-month ramp (e.g., 40/70/140M tokens each month) and the resulting unit price blended? Procurement would like one sample invoice line per month so we can validate cashflow.

If you can get answers back by end of day Thursday (2 Jul), I can circle this with legal and loop our SOW reviewer.

Best,
Olivia
Head of Platform Partnerships — Acme Corporation

Subject: Re: Fwd: Scaled commit playbook + SLA credit outline for Acme — procurement questions

David / Karthik —

High level: proposal looks clean. A few commercial notes before we send back:

1) Quarterly cap on Enterprise credits: Agree to 5% of committed spend per quarter, but set an annual cap at 15% to protect margins if they hit repeated regressions.
2) Dual-region uplift: +3% uplift vs single-region (covers reserved capacity fragmentation). Keep the uplift as optional add-on in SOW.
3) Burst buffer: Recommend default 8% for 48 hours, not 10%/72h — slightly tighter keeps cost exposure down and is simpler for billing. Any excess usage above the buffer should be billed at on-demand rate and applied to committed volume when calculating true-up at month end.

On the sample invoice calc: I reviewed Growth-ramp tab. For a 3-month ramp (40/70/140M) you should show: monthly committed price, on-demand line items for month-1 overage, and the final blended rate after true-up. I can paste a sample line if helpful.

One more ask: mark the proposal as "subject to final SOW and SOC 2 appendix" to keep legal happy.

I'll approve the numbers once the invoice example is included and the buffer/cap values are updated.

-marissa
VP, Revenue — Redwood Inference

Olivia / procurement team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Per our internal review, here's a concise update and the sample invoice lines (attached workbook updated):

1) Enterprise credits: capped at 5% of committed spend per quarter, with an annual cap of 15% of total committed spend.
2) Regional split: supported. If you want dual-region reservation we apply a +3% uplift on committed price. Single-region commitments have no uplift.
3) Burst buffer: default = 8% of monthly committed tokens for a 48-hour window. Bursts beyond this are billed at on-demand rate and any overage is applied to the month true-up. Buffer parameters can be toggled in SOW.

Sample invoice (Growth tier, 3-month ramp):
- Month 1: committed qty 40M @ committed rate $0.0008/token = $32,000; on-demand overage 0 (assumes within buffer)
- Month 2: committed qty 70M @ committed rate $0.00075/token = $52,500; on-demand overage 10M @ $0.0012 = $12,000
- Month 3: committed qty 140M @ committed rate $0.0007/token = $98,000; on-demand overage 20M @ $0.0011 = $22,000

Blended unit price across quarter (committed + overage) example = (32,000 + 52,500 + 12,000 + 98,000 + 22,000) / (40M+70M+140M+overage tokens) => workbook has exact calc and rounding.

Next steps: if the above matches, I’ll:
- Update the workbook to lock the numbers and copy into a clean SOW template
- Send the SOW via DocuSign for your review, marked as "subject to final SOW and SOC 2 appendix"

If Procurement wants a short call to walk the sample invoice, I can make time early next week.

Thanks —
David Kim
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
